# Prolongations of Simple Lie (Super)algebras with Cartan Matrix in Characteristic p > 2

## Abstract/Introduction

This study presents an investigation into the prolongations of simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras and Lie superalgebras possessing a Cartan matrix, defined over algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 2. The central methodological approach involves examining certain simplest, and thereby most tractable, gradings of these algebraic structures. By systematically analyzing these gradings, we develop a prolongation-theoretic framework that allows for the construction and classification of new algebraic objects arising from known simple Lie algebras and superalgebras.

Through the application of this prolongation technique, several previously unknown simple Lie superalgebras have been discovered and rigorously constructed. This collection of new algebras encompasses both serial families—infinite sequences of superalgebras parametrized by rank or dimension—and exceptional types, which stand as isolated structures not fitting into any general series. The existence of these exceptional superalgebras is particularly noteworthy, as it reflects the rich and often unpredictable structure theory that characterizes modular Lie superalgebras, in contrast to the more rigid classification results available in characteristic zero.

Among the most significant results of this investigation are two specific families of superalgebras arising as super-analogues of previously known exceptional simple Lie algebras in prime characteristic: the **superBrown superalgebras** and the **superMelikyan superalgebras**. These constructions extend the classical Brown algebras and Melikyan algebras—themselves exceptional simple Lie algebras that exist only in small positive characteristics—into the super setting, thereby providing new examples of simple Lie superalgebras that have no direct analogues in characteristic zero. The construction of these superalgebras via prolongation methods sheds light on their internal grading structure and root system, and situates them naturally within the broader landscape of modular Lie superalgebra theory.

In addition to these constructive results, this work also provides a systematic classification of all simple Lie superalgebras with a Cartan matrix of rank 2. This classification effort completes an important gap in the structural theory of low-rank Lie superalgebras in positive characteristic, offering a comprehensive list of such algebras together with their defining Cartan matrices, root systems, and relevant structural properties. The rank 2 case, while modest in scope, serves as an essential foundation for understanding higher-rank phenomena and for verifying the completeness of classification schemes proposed for more general settings.

Collectively, these results contribute significantly to the ongoing effort to classify and understand simple Lie superalgebras with Cartan matrix over fields of positive characteristic, a problem that remains considerably more intricate than its characteristic-zero counterpart due to the appearance of exceptional simple objects, non-semisimple prolongations, and subtle interactions between the even and odd parts of the superalgebra under the grading induced by the Cartan matrix.

# Prolongations of Simple Lie Algebras and Superalgebras with Cartan Matrix in Characteristic p > 2

## Introduction

The classification of simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras and Lie superalgebras over fields of positive characteristic has remained one of the most challenging problems in modern algebra, particularly in the "small characteristic" regime where p = 2 or p = 3 introduces phenomena entirely absent in characteristic zero. This study addresses a substantial portion of this problem for characteristic p > 2 by examining a specific but powerful technique: the method of prolongations applied to distinguished gradings of Lie (super)algebras possessing a Cartan matrix.

The Cartan matrix formalism, so successful in the classical theory of semisimple Lie algebras over fields of characteristic zero, extends to modular and super settings but with important caveats. In characteristic p, and especially in the presence of a Z/2Z-grading distinguishing even and odd generators, the structural theory becomes considerably richer. New phenomena emerge: some Lie superalgebras admit Cartan matrices that have no classical analog, some exhibit exceptional behavior only for small primes, and the very notion of simplicity requires careful treatment due to the presence of nontrivial ideals that can arise from restricted structures or from the characteristic itself.

## Methodology: The Prolongation Technique

Our primary tool is the technique of prolongation, applied to what we term the "simplest" gradings of the algebras under consideration. Given a Z-graded Lie (super)algebra

$$\mathfrak{g} = \bigoplus_{i \geq -d} \mathfrak{g}_i$$

with a well-understood non-positive part $\mathfrak{g}_{-} = \bigoplus_{i<0} \mathfrak{g}_i$ and a reductive (or simple) component $\mathfrak{g}_0$, the prolongation procedure reconstructs, or in some cases extends, the full positive part $\mathfrak{g}_+ = \bigoplus_{i>0} \mathfrak{g}_i$ by imposing natural compatibility conditions — essentially requiring that the bracket structure satisfy the Jacobi identity while respecting the action of $\mathfrak{g}_0$ on each graded component.

This method is particularly effective when applied to the simplest possible gradings — those of minimal depth, typically depth 1 or depth 2 — associated with a Cartan matrix. In such gradings, the negative part $\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$ (or $\mathfrak{g}_{-1} \oplus \mathfrak{g}_{-2}$) is an irreducible $\mathfrak{g}_0$-module, and the prolongation is governed by classical invariant-theoretic considerations concerning the module structure. When these gradings are examined over algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 2, the resulting prolongations frequently exceed what is predicted by characteristic-zero intuition: additional terms appear in positive degree due to the existence of divided power algebras, truncated polynomial rings, and other characteristically modular constructions (such as those underlying the Melikyan algebras in the non-super setting).

By systematically applying this prolongation procedure to every simple Lie superalgebra with Cartan matrix (and to the known simple Lie algebras with Cartan matrix in characteristic p), we obtain not merely a verification of existing classifications but a discovery mechanism for new simple objects that had previously escaped detection.

## Main Results: New Simple Lie Superalgebras

The prolongation method applied in this paper yields several new families of simple Lie superalgebras that were previously unknown in the literature. These fall into two broad categories:

### Serial (Infinite) Families

We construct new infinite series of simple Lie superalgebras arising as prolongations of gradings associated with known or previously unclassified Cartan matrices. These serial superalgebras generalize, in a characteristic-dependent fashion, certain vectorial Lie superalgebras of Cartan type, but possess Cartan matrix presentations that make their root-system-theoretic structure transparent. Their existence demonstrates that the classification of simple Lie superalgebras with Cartan matrix in characteristic p > 2 is considerably more intricate than the corresponding classification in characteristic zero (due to Kac), where only a finite list of serial and exceptional superalgebras occurs.

### Exceptional Superalgebras: superBrown and superMelikyan

Among the most striking discoveries of this work are two exceptional simple Lie superalgebras, which we name the **superBrown superalgebra** and the **superMelikyan superalgebra**, in analogy with their non-super antecedents:

- The **superBrown superalgebra** is constructed as the prolongation of a grading whose even part recovers (a version of) the Brown algebra, a simple Lie algebra of characteristic 5 discovered by Brown in the 1980s that has no classical or characteristic-zero counterpart. Our construction extends this exceptional phenomenon into the super setting, producing a Lie superalgebra whose odd part carries an irreducible module structure compatible with the Brown algebra's exceptional 5-dimensional (or appropriately sized) representation.

- The **superMelikyan superalgebra** generalizes the Melikyan algebras, the exceptional simple Lie algebras existing only in characteristic 5 that were discovered by Melikyan and later placed within the Kostrikin–Shafarevich classification program for simple Lie algebras of characteristic p. The super version constructed here via prolongation exhibits an odd part built from divided power algebra constructions twisted by a spinorial-type module, mirroring in the super setting the intricate mixture of Witt algebra and divided power algebra components that characterizes the classical Melikyan construction.

Both of these exceptional superalgebras exist only for the prime p = 5, consistent with the general philosophy that the most exotic simple Lie algebras in prime characteristic tend to be sporadic, tied to a single small prime, and resistant to any uniform construction valid across all primes.

## Classification in Rank 2

Beyond the discovery of new examples, this paper achieves a complete classification of simple Lie superalgebras with Cartan matrix of rank 2 over algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 2. Rank 2 Cartan matrices are combinatorially tractable — there are only finitely many possible matrix types up to the natural equivalences (rescaling, permutation of simple roots, and Cartan matrix symmetries specific to the super setting where off-diagonal entries may vanish in ways impossible in the non-super case) — yet the classification requires careful case-by-case analysis of the prolongation associated to each candidate Cartan matrix, together with a determination of exactly when the prolongation stabilizes (i.e., the positive part $\mathfrak{g}_+$ becomes zero beyond some finite degree) versus when it produces an infinite-dimensional prolongation that must be truncated or does not correspond to a simple finite-dimensional object.

Our classification confirms that in rank 2:

1. All the classical (characteristic-zero) rank 2 simple Lie superalgebras with Cartan matrix persist as simple objects in characteristic p > 2, subject to the expected modular deformations of their structure constants and occasional restriction-related identifications;

2. Several new rank 2 simple Lie superalgebras, not present in characteristic zero, appear precisely for small primes (p = 3, 5, and in some cases 7), arising from the modular collapse of the classical Cartan matrix relations;

3. The exceptional superBrown and superMelikyan superalgebras, while not themselves of rank 2, have rank-2 sub-quotients or truncations that appear naturally within this classification, illustrating the interconnected nature of the exceptional phenomena across different ranks.

This rank 2 classification thus serves both as a self-contained result and as a template for the higher-rank classification problem, illustrating the general prolongation methodology in the simplest nontrivial cases where computations remain fully explicit.

## Conclusion

The results presented in this work substantially advance the classification program for simple Lie algebras and Lie superalgebras with Cartan matrix over algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 2. By systematically exploiting the prolongation technique applied to minimal gradings, we uncover new serial superalgebras, two genuinely new exceptional superalgebras (superBrown and superMelikyan) tied to the prime p = 5, and we resolve completely the rank 2 classification problem. These findings underscore the richness of modular Lie superalgebra theory and set the stage for extending the prolongation methodology to higher ranks, where further exceptional phenomena, tied to yet other small primes, may well await discovery.

# Lie Theory and the Cartan Legacy: Structures Over Fields

The mathematical fields of Lie groups and Lie algebras represent one of the most profound and far-reaching developments in modern mathematics, connecting geometry, algebra, and analysis in ways that continue to influence physics and pure mathematics alike. Central to this rich theory are two towering figures: Sophus Lie, the Norwegian mathematician who first introduced these structures, and Élie Cartan, the French mathematician whose systematic classification work brought the theory to full maturity.

## The Foundations Laid by Sophus Lie

In the late nineteenth century, Sophus Lie developed his theory of continuous transformation groups—now known as Lie groups—as a tool for understanding the symmetries of differential equations. His key insight was that the local structure of these groups could be captured by simpler algebraic objects: Lie algebras. A Lie algebra consists of a vector space equipped with a bilinear bracket operation satisfying antisymmetry and the Jacobi identity. This linearization of group structure allowed mathematicians to study continuous symmetries using the more tractable tools of linear algebra.

## Algebras Over Fields

A crucial aspect of Lie theory involves specifying the field over which these algebraic structures are defined. Lie algebras can be constructed over the real numbers, the complex numbers, or more general fields, and the choice of underlying field profoundly affects the theory's properties. Complex Lie algebras, for instance, admit a cleaner classification theory than their real counterparts, since algebraic closure simplifies the analysis of eigenvalues and root systems. Understanding a Lie algebra "over" a particular field means recognizing how scalar multiplication interacts with the bracket operation, and how the field's arithmetic properties—such as characteristic or algebraic closure—shape the algebra's representation theory and structural classification.

## Cartan's Systematic Classification

Building on Wilhelm Killing's earlier work, Élie Cartan achieved a complete classification of simple Lie algebras over the complex numbers, organizing them into four infinite families (types A, B, C, D) alongside five exceptional algebras (G2, F4, E6, E7, E8). This classification relied heavily on the concept now known as a Cartan subalgebra—a maximal abelian subalgebra consisting of semisimple elements, through which one can analyze the algebra's root system.

Cartan's method involved decomposing a Lie algebra into eigenspaces relative to the adjoint action of a Cartan subalgebra, producing a root system that encodes the algebra's entire structure. This elegant correspondence between abstract algebraic objects and combinatorial-geometric data (root systems, Dynkin diagrams) represents one of mathematics' most beautiful classification theorems.

## Enduring Influence

The interplay between Lie's foundational insights and Cartan's structural classification created a framework that extends far beyond pure mathematics. Today, Lie algebras over various fields appear throughout theoretical physics—in quantum mechanics, gauge theory, and string theory—as well as in differential geometry, representation theory, and algebraic geometry. The precision with which Cartan characterized these structures over the complex numbers, and later extended his methods to real forms and symmetric spaces, continues to serve as a cornerstone for mathematical research well over a century after these ideas were first developed.

# Abstract

Let $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{g}_{-1} \oplus \mathfrak{g}_0 \oplus \mathfrak{g}_1$ be a $\mathbb{Z}$-graded Lie algebra or Lie superalgebra of depth one over an algebraically closed field $K$ of characteristic $p > 2$. We study the Cartan prolongation
$$
(\mathfrak{g}_{-1}, \mathfrak{g}_0)_* = \bigoplus_{i \geq -1} \mathfrak{g}_i
$$
in the setting where $\mathfrak{g}_0$ acts on $\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$ as a classical or modular simple Lie algebra (respectively, simple Lie superalgebra) with an indecomposable Cartan matrix, and $\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$ is taken to be an irreducible $\mathfrak{g}_0$-module arising naturally from the defining representation associated with the Cartan matrix structure.

For each simple Lie algebra and Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{g}_0$ with Cartan matrix in characteristic $p>2$—including the classical series, the Cartan-type and Melikian algebras' finite-dimensional building blocks realizable this way, and their super-analogues such as the periplectic, orthosymplectic and exceptional series—we determine explicitly the depth, height, and full graded structure of the resulting prolongation $\mathfrak{g}_i$ for all $i$. We show that in characteristic $p$ these prolongations frequently truncate at low degree, in sharp contrast with the characteristic zero picture, and we identify precisely when the prolongation is finite-dimensional, giving explicit bounds on its height in terms of $p$ and the rank of the Cartan matrix.

As an application we classify the resulting simple graded Lie (super)algebras obtained by taking the prolongation together with a suitable truncation or the derived subalgebra of the non-truncated part, thereby producing new families of finite-dimensional simple modular Lie superalgebras of Cartan type. We also describe the restricted structures (where they exist) on these prolongations and discuss their relation to known deformation families and to the classification problem of simple Lie superalgebras over algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p>2$. The results extend and unify earlier prolongation constructions of Kac, Kostrikin–Shafarevich, and Skryabin to the Cartan-matrix graded setting in the modular case, providing a systematic tool for constructing new simple objects and for understanding restrictions imposed by positive characteristic on classical prolongation phenomena.

# Simple Lie Superalgebras from Prolongation Methods in Positive Characteristic

## Overview

Cartan prolongation techniques—originally developed for classifying simple Lie algebras of vector fields—have been extended to the super setting in positive characteristic (typically p = 2, 3, 5), yielding new families of simple Lie superalgebras that lack classical (characteristic 0) analogues. This work extends the modular Lie algebra classification program (Kostrikin–Shafarevich, Block–Wilson–Premet–Strade) into the super context.

## Key Methodology

The prolongation approach constructs Lie superalgebras by:
1. Starting with a **finite-dimensional irreducible representation** (often of a classical or Cartan-type Lie superalgebra) as a "negative part" or degree −1 component
2. Computing the **full prolongation** — the maximal Lie superalgebra containing this piece consistently with a compatible grading
3. Truncating using **divided power (Jacobson–Witt type) constructions** appropriate to positive characteristic, since ordinary polynomial prolongations often become infinite-dimensional there without truncation

This mirrors the classical Cartan prolongation of e.g. 𝔰𝔩(n) or 𝔰𝔭(2n) acting on their standard modules, which recovers the Lie algebras of vector fields W(n), S(n), H(2n), K(2n+1).

## New Superalgebra Families

### Brown-type Superalgebras
The **Brown algebra** in characteristic 5 is a 25-dimensional simple Lie algebra arising as a prolongation related to the contact/Hamiltonian structure with an exceptional grading, not fitting the standard Cartan-type W, S, H, K families. Super-analogues have been constructed by:
- Taking odd super-partners of the Brown algebra's building blocks
- Using a prolongation of a suitable 𝔬𝔰𝔭 or exceptional module in characteristic 5
- Producing new simple **Lie superalgebras with no counterpart in characteristic 0**, whose even parts recover Brown-type or related exceptional algebras and whose odd parts form new irreducible modules tied to the p = 5 restriction

### Melikyan-type Superalgebras
The classical **Melikyan algebra** (characteristic 5) is built via prolongation combining the Witt algebra W(2;\underline{n}) with the contact algebra K(3;\underline{n}), producing an exceptional simple Lie algebra with no analogue in other characteristics. Its super-generalizations:
- Extend the Melikyan construction by superizing the special/Hamiltonian pieces used in the prolongation
- Yield **simple Lie superalgebras specific to characteristic 5**, with even part isomorphic (or closely related) to Melikyan-type or deformed Hamiltonian algebras, and odd part given by spinor-type or exterior-power modules
- Depend sensitively on the characteristic-5 identities (e.g., relations among p-th powers, restricted structures) that make the classical Melikyan algebra exceptional

## Structural Features of the New Algebras

- **Restricted/non-restricted variants**: Many arise as non-restricted simple Lie superalgebras, requiring careful treatment of the p-mapping (restriction) on the even part
- **Filtered deformations**: Some new superalgebras appear as filtered deformations of graded Cartan-type superalgebras, analogous to how the Brown and Melikyan algebras deform gradations of Hamiltonian/contact types
- **Exceptional gradings**: The prolongations exploit gradings not available in char 0, e.g. depth exceeding the usual bound of 2, tied to the vanishing of certain identities specific to small p
- **Classification refinement**: These examples show that the analogue of the Kostrikin–Shafarevich conjecture (that all simple modular Lie algebras are of classical or Cartan type) fails even more dramatically in the super setting — prolongation methods generate additional exceptional families beyond even the Melikyan/Brown exceptions known in the non-super case

## Significance

These results indicate:
- The classification of simple modular Lie superalgebras is **richer and more exceptional-laden** than the Lie algebra case
- Prolongation remains a **powerful constructive tool** for discovering new simple objects, complementing (and going beyond) the deformation and cohomological methods used elsewhere in modular Lie theory
- The new algebras provide test cases for extending structure theory (Cartan-type classification, restricted enveloping algebra theory, cohomology) to the small-characteristic super setting, where many characteristic-0 tools (Killing form nondegeneracy, semisimplicity criteria) fail

## Caveat

This area is technical and part of an active research program (work associated with Bouarroudj, Grozman, Leites, and collaborators on modular Lie superalgebra classification). Precise dimension counts, explicit multiplication tables, and full classification statements should be checked against the primary papers, as conventions for prolongation and grading vary and the field continues to be actively refined.

# Classification of Simple Lie Superalgebras with Cartan Matrix of Rank 2 in Characteristic p > 2

## Abstract

We present a complete classification of finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebras of rank 2 possessing a Cartan matrix over algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p > 2$. This work extends the modular Lie algebra classification program to the super setting, revealing phenomena absent both in characteristic zero and in the characteristic-$p$ theory of ordinary Lie algebras.

A Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{g}_{\bar 0} \oplus \mathfrak{g}_{\bar 1}$ admits a Cartan matrix presentation when it can be constructed via generators and relations from a matrix $A = (a_{ij})$ analogous to the classical Chevalley–Serre construction, with a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-grading of simple roots distinguishing even and odd generators. In rank 2, the Cartan matrix is a $2\times 2$ matrix, and the associated root system, while still governed by a rank-2 lattice, exhibits a richer combinatorial structure due to the possible presence of odd isotropic roots satisfying $a_{ii} = 0$.

Our classification proceeds by analyzing the possible Dynkin diagrams (with nodes colored white, black, or gray according to parity and isotropy) compatible with rank-2 root systems, followed by verification of the Serre-type relations and computation of the resulting finite-dimensional quotients. The characteristic $p>2$ setting introduces substantial new features:

1. **Modular exceptions and degenerations**: For small primes ($p=3,5$), several Cartan matrices give rise to superalgebras with deformed structure constants or exceptional isomorphisms not present in characteristic 0, including cases where the "generic" simple quotient degenerates or splits into different structures.

2. **Restricted vs. non-restricted forms**: We identify which rank-2 Cartan matrix superalgebras admit restricted Lie superalgebra structures ($p$-structures on $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar 0}$) and classify the associated $p$-envelopes.

3. **New simple superalgebras**: Beyond the characteristic-0 analogues of $\mathfrak{sl}(2|1)$, $\mathfrak{osp}(3|2)$, $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)\otimes\mathfrak{sl}(2)$, and Cartan-type rank 2 superalgebras, we exhibit modular-specific simple superalgebras arising from Cartan matrices with entries satisfying nontrivial relations modulo $p$, including brown superalgebras and their relatives, which have no characteristic-zero counterpart.

4. **Isomorphism classes**: We resolve the equivalence problem between superalgebras obtained from Cartan matrices related by odd reflections, establishing which matrices yield isomorphic algebras and providing canonical representatives for each isomorphism class.

The resulting classification table lists, for each prime $p > 2$, the complete list of rank-2 Cartan matrices $A$, the corresponding simple superalgebra $\mathfrak{g}(A)$, its dimension, the dimensions of $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar 0}$ and $\mathfrak{g}_{\bar 1}$, and its relation (via central extensions, quotients by center, or exceptional isomorphisms) to classical Lie superalgebras and to Cartan-type superalgebras $\mathfrak{o}(2|2)$, $\mathfrak{s}(2|2)^{(1)}$, and the Kaplansky-type superalgebras $K(1,2)$, $K(3)$ where applicable in low rank.

This classification serves as foundational data for the broader project of classifying all finite-dimensional simple modular Lie superalgebras, complementing existing results for Lie algebras (Block–Wilson–Premet–Strade) and providing the base cases for inductive rank arguments in higher-rank Cartan matrix superalgebras.

**Keywords:** Lie superalgebras, Cartan matrix, modular representation theory, characteristic $p$, simple superalgebras, root systems, Serre relations

# Abstract

The classification of gradings on simple Lie algebras and superalgebras constitutes a fundamental problem with deep connections to representation theory, invariant theory, and the structure theory of algebraic groups. In this work, we undertake a systematic investigation of fine gradings on simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras and Lie superalgebras possessing a Cartan matrix, extending known classification techniques to the graded setting for both classical and exceptional families.

Our approach combines the theory of maximal tori in automorphism group schemes with explicit computational methods for constructing and verifying gradings compatible with the root space decomposition induced by a Cartan matrix. By systematically analyzing the interplay between even and odd parts of the superalgebra under a grading, we identify obstructions and compatibility conditions that must be satisfied for a consistent $\mathbb{Z}^n$- or more general abelian group grading to exist.

Applying this methodology across the known families of simple Lie superalgebras with Cartan matrix — including the classical series $\mathfrak{sl}(m|n)$, $\mathfrak{osp}(m|2n)$, and the exceptional superalgebras $D(2,1;\alpha)$, $G(3)$, and $F(4)$ — we recover all previously known fine gradings and, more significantly, uncover several new gradings not documented in the prior literature. Notably, our analysis reveals the existence of two new exceptional-type gradings tied to hitherto unexplored torus embeddings, as well as a new infinite series of gradings arising from a modified diagonal embedding compatible with the odd root spaces.

These results are supported by explicit computations of the corresponding Weyl groups of the gradings, universal grading groups, and moduli of the associated fine gradings up to equivalence. We further discuss the implications of these new gradings for the classification of graded contractions, graded modules, and the associated graded Lie algebra cohomology. Our findings not only complete several open cases in the classification program of gradings on Lie superalgebras but also point toward new structural phenomena distinguishing the graded theory of superalgebras from that of ordinary Lie algebras, suggesting promising directions for future research into graded representation theory and generalized root systems.

**Abstract**

We investigate prolongations of Cartan-type matrix Lie superalgebras over algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 2, extending the classification theory of simple Lie superalgebras to positive characteristic settings. Starting from the negative parts constructed from classical and Cartan-type Lie superalgebras, we compute the full prolongations and determine their structure as infinite-dimensional or finite-dimensional simple Lie superalgebras, depending on the grading and the choice of matrix data. Particular attention is given to two exceptional families arising in low characteristic: the superBrown superalgebras, a super-analogue of the exceptional Brown algebras appearing in characteristic 5, and the superMelikyan superalgebras, generalizing the exceptional Melikyan Lie algebras of characteristic 5 to the super setting. We describe their root space decompositions, identify their even and odd parts in terms of known Cartan-type superalgebras, and verify their simplicity. These results provide new examples of modular Lie superalgebras that do not have classical (characteristic 0) analogues, thereby enriching the classification of simple Lie superalgebras over fields of small positive characteristic and clarifying the interplay between prolongation techniques and exceptional phenomena specific to characteristic 5.
